title: India's Global Market Cap Share Drops Below 3% for First Time in Four Years
excerpt: Foreign investor exodus and Middle East turmoil shrink India's stock market valuation to $4.91 trillion, down from a peak share of 4.71% in September 2024
body:
India's stock market just crossed an uncomfortable threshold. The country's share of global market capitalization slipped below 3% for the first time since 2022, settling at 2.996% as of May 11 — a stark reversal from the heady 4.71% peak reached in September 2024 when Dalal Street seemed unstoppable.

**The Numbers Tell the Story:** India's total market capitalization now stands at approximately $4.91 trillion, down roughly 7% from recent highs. The decline has been driven by a relentless outflow of foreign portfolio investment — FPIs have pulled out over $23 billion in 2025 alone, with another ₹14,231 crore withdrawn in May. According to Motilal Oswal, this marks a 14-year low in FPI holdings as a share of Indian markets.

**Why the Exodus:** The triggers are both global and local. The US-Iran conflict has sent crude oil past $100 a barrel, hammering India's import-dependent economy. The rupee's slide to record lows compounds the pain for dollar-denominated foreign investors, who face currency losses on top of equity declines. Meanwhile, competing markets have surged — China's global share climbed to 9.6%, while South Korea and Taiwan, buoyed by the AI semiconductor boom, each approached 3%, effectively catching up with India.

**The Domestic Drag:** India's Sensex has shed roughly 11 lakh crore in recent weeks. The Budget's STT hike on derivatives trading in February spooked sentiment early in the year, and successive shocks — from geopolitical tensions to a weakening currency — have prevented any sustained recovery. Analysts at Multibagg note five overlapping triggers: West Asia tensions, rising crude, rupee weakness, elevated US bond yields, and sustained foreign selling.

**The NRI Investor's Dilemma:** For the millions of Indian-Americans with investment portfolios split between US and Indian markets, the divergence is painful. Indian equities have underperformed virtually every major global peer in FY26, logging their steepest annual decline in three years. NRIs who invested in Indian mutual funds or direct equities during the 2024 rally are sitting on significant losses, compounded by the rupee's depreciation which erodes returns when converted back to dollars.

**A Silver Lining?** Some analysts see opportunity in the correction. India's long-term growth story — young demographics, digital infrastructure, manufacturing ambitions — remains intact. Domestic institutional investors continue to provide a floor, and valuations are finally approaching reasonable levels after years of premium pricing. The question is whether geopolitical headwinds will abate before retail patience runs out.

**What to Watch:** FPI flow data over the next month will signal whether the selling is exhaustion or acceleration. A de-escalation in the Middle East and oil's retreat below $100 would be the most powerful catalyst for a reversal.
nri_angle: NRIs with Indian equity portfolios face a double hit: market declines plus rupee depreciation erode dollar-denominated returns. The correction may offer a buying opportunity for long-term diaspora investors willing to ride out geopolitical volatility.
author: Diaspora Desk
